name: Valley Health
blurb: Two hospitals and nine clinics, about 6,000 nurses and techs, and a rural clinic in Marrow Creek that serves 11,000 people. Founder Dr. Evelyn Marsh built it from that single clinic and her family trust still holds 22% of the vote.

exposure.text: Disbarred if the board is caught burying while he sits on it.

secrets.text: Never be on a board that's caught burying.
Your firm holds the system's compliance contract. An independent investigator would replace you, so none gets hired.

exposure.text: Loses the next vote if more than 10% of nurses and techs are cut, or patient loads per nurse go up.

secrets.text: The safe-staffing ratio gets funded before the game ends.
You were granted stock options last year. The stock must end above where it started.

exposure.text: Investors pull money from her fund if the stock ends below where it started.

secrets.text: Pass a distribution of $40M or more in any round. After that you may resign.
Your fund quietly owns a rival hospital chain. Valley Health's stock must finish in the bottom half.

directors.name: Dr. Arthur Penn
directors.title: Founder's friend
directors.home: Dr. Evelyn Marsh, the founder (residency classmate)

exposure.text: Loses the seat if the board ever votes against something Dr. Marsh wants.

secrets.text: Dr. Marsh approved the new billing codes. Make sure the board never votes Tell on them.
You sit on two other boards. No scandal anywhere you sit, so no disclosure on this board gets caught.

exposure.text: Loses standing at home if the board closes the rural clinic, cuts nurses, or raises patient loads per nurse.

secrets.text: Either the safe-staffing ratio or the rural mobile clinic passes.
You would run the consolidated hospital if the rural clinic closes. Get the closure through.

motions.title: Distribution to owners and bondholders
motions.motive: Return the surplus to the people who funded us, and the market will notice tonight.

motions.title: Safe-staffing ratio of five patients per nurse
motions.motive: Nobody should carry more than five patients on a night shift.

motions.title: Publish prices in plain English
motions.motive: Patients should know the cost before they sign.

motions.title: Mobile clinic for rural roads
motions.motive: Bring the exam room to people who live an hour out.

motions.title: Rate cut for insurers who pay early
motions.motive: Faster payments help our cash and their books.

motions.title: Open a new cardiology wing
motions.motive: Heart patients come with good coverage and bring other work with them.

issue.text: An internal review found billing codes bumped up on about one in eight inpatient stays. It adds roughly $14M a year. Only the review team has seen it.
issue.tell: Report it to insurers and repay; small stock dip now.
issue.bury: Say nothing. If the Auditor or Reporter finds it, the stock drops hard and the Attorney is exposed. Nothing the board buys this round removes the problem.

motions.title: AI triage at every intake desk, cut 20% of triage staff
motions.motive: Every system will do this, and waiting just makes us the slow one.

motions.title: AI triage with nurse review, retrain staff
motions.motive: Use the tool and keep the people who know the patient.

motions.title: Use the AI for scheduling and billing only
motions.motive: No change at the front door. Nobody loses a job.

motions.title: Hold off on AI triage this year
motions.motive: Wait and see what breaks at other systems first.

motions.title: Mandatory sepsis check at every intake
motions.motive: A nurse runs the screen no matter what the software says.

motions.title: Sell de-identified patient records to researchers
motions.motive: They're stripped of names. Others pay for them.

issue.text: In testing, the AI triage pilot missed 9 of 40 sepsis cases that nurses caught. The vendor knows. The system plans to extend the pilot to the rural clinics next month.
issue.tell: Publish the results and pause the pilot at the rural clinics.
issue.spin: "Pilot performance is within expected variability for a new system."
issue.bury: Say nothing and extend the pilot. If full triage deployment passed this round, the odds of someone finding it go up.

rounds.brief: Find $26M in savings this round. Only $8M to spend on anything new.

motions.title: Close the Marrow Creek rural clinic
motions.motive: Low volume, high cost, and the lease ends in March.

motions.title: Lay off 15% of nurses and techs
Raise patient loads to seven per nurse
Cancel this year's distribution
motions.motive: Owners share the bad year too.

motions.title: Push equipment replacement to next year
motions.motive: The machines still work. The purchase can wait.

motions.title: Telehealth line for rural patients
motions.motive: A nurse on a screen is better than an hour's drive.

issue.text: The system plans to close the Marrow Creek rural clinic, which serves 11,000 people, and hasn't announced it. The lease ends in March.
issue.tell: Announce it now and hold public hearings; stock dips now.
issue.spin: "We are exploring care-delivery options for the Marrow Creek area."

design_note: Savings that fire no exposure are cut_distribution 8 + exec_pay 3 + defer_equipment 7 = 18, below 26; nurse_layoff and raise_ratios fire Teresa and Imani, and close_clinic fires Imani, so every legal package fires someone.
